activity_context.topic_title: Writing Sums of Trigonometric Functions in Amplitude-Phase Form

feedback.problem: Given that the expression $2\sqrt{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with $0<ϕ<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\sqrt{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\sqrt{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{6} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{2\sqrt{6}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\ ϕ & =\frac{\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
